admission.justification: The two witness scripts separate complete discovery equivalence from bounded startup timing and record execution attribution, preventing tool counts or the wrong checkout interpreter from being presented as a preserved contract.

applicability: The two repository scripts and their explicit scratch subprocess worlds. The proposed 5s/20CPU/load<=40 bound is a measured condition, not a host-independent runtime guarantee.
conditions: The scripts execute their own ordinary/explainer subprocess world without calling a tool.
Discovery compares canonical complete tools/list answers and reports actual executed-source attribution.
Timing records spawn-to-response, load, command, dependencies, source and cache facts.
exclusions: Runtime refusals, installed acceptance, first-call runtime effects or any-load timing guarantees.
Reporting an over-load witness as representative or adjacency of a venv as proof of executed source.
statement: Startup and discovery witnesses retain their actual execution source and limits: discovery compares complete canonical tools/list results rather than counts, while startup timing measures spawn through initialize and completed tools/list without a tool call and records load/source/dependency/cache facts; neither witness substitutes for runtime refusal tests or installed acceptance.
